## Training and Test datasets

```{r}
set.seed(1)
library(gbm)      # For Gradient Boosting
library(class)
library(caTools)
library(ROCR)
library(caret)
library(vip)  # For feature importance
library(gridExtra)

set.seed(1)
## Data partitioning for caret library
#levels(all_data$sample$undocu_likely) <- make.names(levels(all_data$sample$undocu_likely))
train_index_gbm <- createDataPartition(sipp08_2_wmissing$undocu_likely, p = 0.7, list = FALSE)
train_gbm <- sipp08_2_wmissing[train_index_gbm, ]
test_gbm <- sipp08_2_wmissing[-train_index_gbm, ]

```

```{r}
# Create the grid
my_grid <- expand.grid(
  shrinkage = c(0.01, 0.005),
  interaction.depth = c(4, 6, 8)
)

# Empty vector to store results
cv_errors <- numeric(nrow(my_grid))
optimal_trees <- numeric(nrow(my_grid))

set.seed(1)
for(i in 1:nrow(my_grid)) {
  
  # Train a temporary model with the grid's current row settings
  temp_model <- gbm(
    undocu_likely ~ age + fem + married + cit_spouse + medicaid + nonfluent + spanish_hispanic_latino + central_latino + bpl_asia + household_size + poverty + race + employed + years_us + yrsed, 
    data = train_gbm,
    distribution = "bernoulli",
    verbose = FALSE,
    cv.folds = 10,
    n.trees = 5000, # Set a high ceiling, cv will find the optimum
    shrinkage = my_grid$shrinkage[i],
    interaction.depth = my_grid$interaction.depth[i]
  )
  
  # Find the optimal trees for this specific combination
  opt_t <- gbm.perf(temp_model, method = "cv", plot.it = FALSE)
  
  # Store the lowest CV error achieved and the number of trees it took
  cv_errors[i] <- temp_model$cv.error[opt_t]
  optimal_trees[i] <- opt_t
  
  cat("Finished grid row", i, "of", nrow(my_grid), "\n")
}

# Bind results and find the winner
my_grid$min_cv_error <- cv_errors
my_grid$optimal_trees <- optimal_trees
best_params <- my_grid[which.min(my_grid$min_cv_error), ]
print(best_params)
```

```{r}
# Assuming you just ran the loop and have this object:

set.seed(1)
best_model <- gbm(

  data = train_gbm,
  distribution = "bernoulli", # Assuming binary classification
  verbose = FALSE,
  
  # --- Injecting the optimized parameters here ---
  n.trees = best_params$optimal_trees, 
  shrinkage = best_params$shrinkage, 
  interaction.depth = best_params$interaction.depth
)

# Check the final model summary
print(best_model)
```

##  XGBoost

```{r}
# Install if necessary: install.packages(c("xgboost", "Matrix"))
library(xgboost)
library(Matrix)
library(dplyr)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Data Preparation (The Bulletproof XGBoost Way)
# ==============================================================================

# 1. Extract and force labels to numeric vectors
train_y <- as.numeric(train_gbm$undocu_likely)
test_y <- as.numeric(test_gbm$undocu_likely)

# 2. Extract features, force all to numeric, and convert straight to matrix
train_matrix <- train_gbm %>% 
  select(age, fem, married, cit_spouse, medicaid, nonfluent, 
         spanish_hispanic_latino, central_latino, bpl_asia, household_size, 
         poverty, asian, black, white, other_race, employed, years_us, yrsed) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>% 
  as.matrix()

test_matrix <- test_gbm %>% 
  select(age, fem, married, cit_spouse, medicaid, nonfluent, 
         spanish_hispanic_latino, central_latino, bpl_asia, household_size, 
         poverty, asian, black, white, other_race, employed, years_us, yrsed) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>% 
  as.matrix()

# 3. Create XGBoost DMatrix objects
# Because as.matrix() never drops rows, nrow(train_matrix) == length(train_y) 
# is now guaranteed to be TRUE.
dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(data = train_matrix, label = train_y)
dtest <- xgb.DMatrix(data = test_matrix, label = test_y)


# ==============================================================================
# 2. Define the Grid Search
# ==============================================================================

# XGBoost uses different names: eta = shrinkage, max_depth = interaction.depth
xgb_grid <- expand.grid(
  eta = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.1),            # Learning rate
  max_depth = c(4, 6, 8),              # Tree complexity
  subsample = c(0.8, 1.0),             # % of rows used per tree (prevents overfitting)
  colsample_bytree = c(0.8, 1.0)       # % of columns used per tree (prevents overfitting)
)

# Placeholders for results
xgb_grid$optimal_trees <- 0
xgb_grid$max_cv_auc <- 0

cat("Starting XGBoost Grid Search (", nrow(xgb_grid), " combinations)...\n")


# ==============================================================================
# 3. Grid Search via Cross-Validation (Updated)
# ==============================================================================

set.seed(1)
for(i in 1:nrow(xgb_grid)) {
  
  params <- list(
    objective = "binary:logistic",
    eval_metric = "auc",
    eta = xgb_grid$eta[i],
    max_depth = xgb_grid$max_depth[i],
    subsample = xgb_grid$subsample[i],
    colsample_bytree = xgb_grid$colsample_bytree[i]
  )
  
  cv_results <- xgb.cv(
    params = params,
    data = dtrain,
    nrounds = 5000,                    
    nfold = 5,                         
    early_stopping_rounds = 50,  
    maximize = TRUE,                   # EXPLICITLY tell XGBoost that higher AUC is better
    verbose = 0                        
  )
  
  # Extract the evaluation log
  eval_log <- cv_results$evaluation_log
  
  # THE FIX: Find the maximum AUC and the exact row (iteration) it occurred on
  xgb_grid$max_cv_auc[i] <- max(eval_log$test_auc_mean)
  xgb_grid$optimal_trees[i] <- which.max(eval_log$test_auc_mean) 
  
  cat("Finished row", i, "| Optimal Trees:", xgb_grid$optimal_trees[i], 
      "| Best CV AUC:", round(xgb_grid$max_cv_auc[i], 4), "\n")
}


# ==============================================================================
# 4. Extract Winner and Train Final Model
# ==============================================================================

# Find the row with the highest AUC
best_xgb_params <- xgb_grid[which.max(xgb_grid$max_cv_auc), ]

cat("\n=== Best XGBoost Parameters ===\n")
print(best_xgb_params)

# Define the final parameter list using the winning values
final_xgb_params <- list(
  objective = "binary:logistic",
  eval_metric = "auc",
  eta = best_xgb_params$eta,
  max_depth = best_xgb_params$max_depth,
  subsample = best_xgb_params$subsample,
  colsample_bytree = best_xgb_params$colsample_bytree
)

# Train the final model on 100% of the training data
set.seed(1)
xgb_model <- xgb.train(
  params = final_xgb_params,
  data = dtrain,
  nrounds = best_xgb_params$optimal_trees, # Exact optimal stopping point
  verbose = 0
)


# ==============================================================================
# 5. Make Predictions
# ==============================================================================

# predict() in xgboost automatically returns a clean, flat vector of probabilities
# so it won't trigger the matrix/array errors you saw in ROCR earlier.
xgb_pred_probs <- predict(xgb_model, newdata = dtest)

# You can now immediately drop this into your existing ROCR evaluation block:
# rocr_pred_xgb <- prediction(xgb_pred_probs, test_y)
```

## Performance

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# 0. XGBoost Test Data Prep (College Sample)
# ==============================================================================
# We need to create a DMatrix for the college test set before predicting
test_college_matrix <- test_college %>% 
  select(age, fem, married, cit_spouse, medicaid, nonfluent, 
         spanish_hispanic_latino, central_latino, bpl_asia, household_size, 
         poverty, asian, black, white, other_race, employed, years_us, yrsed) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>% 
  as.matrix()

dtest_college <- xgb.DMatrix(data = test_college_matrix, label = as.numeric(test_college$undocu_likely))

# ==============================================================================
# Model Comparisons: ROC, Precision-Recall, and F1 Score (3 Models)
# ==============================================================================
library(ROCR)

# --- 1. Calculate Probabilities & ROCR Prediction Objects ---

# Base Model
pred_probs_ff <- predict(gbm_model, newdata = test_gbm, 
                         n.trees = optimal_trees_gbm, type = "response")
rocr_pred_ff <- prediction(pred_probs_ff, test_gbm$undocu_likely)

pred_probs_fc <- predict(gbm_model, newdata = test_college, 
                         n.trees = optimal_trees_gbm, type = "response")
rocr_pred_fc <- prediction(pred_probs_fc, test_college$undocu_likely)

# Contending Model (Best GBM)
pred_probs_best_ff <- predict(best_model, newdata = test_gbm, 
                              n.trees = best_params$optimal_trees, type = "response")
rocr_pred_best_ff <- prediction(pred_probs_best_ff, test_gbm$undocu_likely)

pred_probs_best_fc <- predict(best_model, newdata = test_college, 
                              n.trees = best_params$optimal_trees, type = "response")
rocr_pred_best_fc <- prediction(pred_probs_best_fc, test_college$undocu_likely)

# XGBoost Model
pred_probs_xgb_ff <- predict(xgb_model, newdata = dtest)
rocr_pred_xgb_ff <- prediction(pred_probs_xgb_ff, test_gbm$undocu_likely)

pred_probs_xgb_fc <- predict(xgb_model, newdata = dtest_college)
rocr_pred_xgb_fc <- prediction(pred_probs_xgb_fc, test_college$undocu_likely)


# --- 2. Calculate Performance Metrics ---

# ROC (True Positive Rate vs False Positive Rate)
roc_ff <- performance(rocr_pred_ff, "tpr", "fpr")
roc_fc <- performance(rocr_pred_fc, "tpr", "fpr")
roc_best_ff <- performance(rocr_pred_best_ff, "tpr", "fpr")
roc_best_fc <- performance(rocr_pred_best_fc, "tpr", "fpr")
roc_xgb_ff <- performance(rocr_pred_xgb_ff, "tpr", "fpr")
roc_xgb_fc <- performance(rocr_pred_xgb_fc, "tpr", "fpr")

# Precision-Recall
pr_ff <- performance(rocr_pred_ff, "prec", "rec")
pr_fc <- performance(rocr_pred_fc, "prec", "rec")
pr_best_ff <- performance(rocr_pred_best_ff, "prec", "rec")
pr_best_fc <- performance(rocr_pred_best_fc, "prec", "rec")
pr_xgb_ff <- performance(rocr_pred_xgb_ff, "prec", "rec")
pr_xgb_fc <- performance(rocr_pred_xgb_fc, "prec", "rec")

# F1 Score (F-measure across all classification cutoffs)
f1_ff <- performance(rocr_pred_ff, "f")
f1_fc <- performance(rocr_pred_fc, "f")
f1_best_ff <- performance(rocr_pred_best_ff, "f")
f1_best_fc <- performance(rocr_pred_best_fc, "f")
f1_xgb_ff <- performance(rocr_pred_xgb_ff, "f")
f1_xgb_fc <- performance(rocr_pred_xgb_fc, "f")


# --- 3. Generate Average Metrics Summary Table ---

calc_f1_05 <- function(pred_probs, actuals) {
  preds <- ifelse(pred_probs > 0.5, 1, 0)
  tp <- sum(preds == 1 & actuals == 1)
  fp <- sum(preds == 1 & actuals == 0)
  fn <- sum(preds == 0 & actuals == 1)
  precision <- tp / (tp + fp)
  recall <- tp / (tp + fn)
  2 * (precision * recall) / (precision + recall)
}

calc_auc_pr <- function(pr_obj) {
  x <- as.numeric(pr_obj@x.values[[1]])
  y <- as.numeric(pr_obj@y.values[[1]])
  valid <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(y)
  x <- x[valid]; y <- y[valid]
  sum(diff(x) * (y[-1] + y[-length(y)]) / 2) 
}

metrics_table <- data.frame(
  Model_Context = c("Base GBM (Full to Full)", "Base GBM (Full to College)", 
                    "Best GBM (Full to Full)", "Best GBM (Full to College)",
                    "XGBoost (Full to Full)", "XGBoost (Full to College)"),
  AUC_ROC = c(
    performance(rocr_pred_ff, "auc")@y.values[[1]],
    performance(rocr_pred_fc, "auc")@y.values[[1]],
    performance(rocr_pred_best_ff, "auc")@y.values[[1]],
    performance(rocr_pred_best_fc, "auc")@y.values[[1]],
    performance(rocr_pred_xgb_ff, "auc")@y.values[[1]],
    performance(rocr_pred_xgb_fc, "auc")@y.values[[1]]
  ),
  AUC_PR = c(
    calc_auc_pr(pr_ff), calc_auc_pr(pr_fc),
    calc_auc_pr(pr_best_ff), calc_auc_pr(pr_best_fc),
    calc_auc_pr(pr_xgb_ff), calc_auc_pr(pr_xgb_fc)
  ),
  F1_at_0.5 = c(
    calc_f1_05(pred_probs_ff, test_gbm$undocu_likely),
    calc_f1_05(pred_probs_fc, test_college$undocu_likely),
    calc_f1_05(pred_probs_best_ff, test_gbm$undocu_likely),
    calc_f1_05(pred_probs_best_fc, test_college$undocu_likely),
    calc_f1_05(pred_probs_xgb_ff, test_gbm$undocu_likely),
    calc_f1_05(pred_probs_xgb_fc, test_college$undocu_likely)
  )
)

print("=== Metric Comparison Table ===")
metrics_table[, 2:4] <- round(metrics_table[, 2:4], 4)
print(metrics_table)


# --- 4. Plotting (Each Metric on its Own Plot) ---

# Using color families to distinguish models: Base=Blues, Best=Greens, XGB=Reds
plot_colors <- c("blue", "dodgerblue", "darkgreen", "limegreen", "darkred", "orange")
plot_legends <- c("Base: Full-Full", "Base: Full-College", 
                  "Best GBM: Full-Full", "Best GBM: Full-College",
                  "XGBoost: Full-Full", "XGBoost: Full-College")
plot_lines <- rep(1, 6) # All solid lines

# Plot 1: ROC Curves
plot(roc_ff, col = plot_colors[1], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[1], main = "ROC Curves")
plot(roc_fc, col = plot_colors[2], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[2], add = TRUE)
plot(roc_best_ff, col = plot_colors[3], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[3], add = TRUE)
plot(roc_best_fc, col = plot_colors[4], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[4], add = TRUE)
plot(roc_xgb_ff, col = plot_colors[5], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[5], add = TRUE)
plot(roc_xgb_fc, col = plot_colors[6], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[6], add = TRUE)
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lty = 2, col = "gray") 
legend("bottomright", legend = plot_legends, col = plot_colors, lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines, cex = 0.7)

# Plot 2: Precision-Recall Curves
plot(pr_ff, col = plot_colors[1], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[1], main = "Precision-Recall Curves")
plot(pr_fc, col = plot_colors[2], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[2], add = TRUE)
plot(pr_best_ff, col = plot_colors[3], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[3], add = TRUE)
plot(pr_best_fc, col = plot_colors[4], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[4], add = TRUE)
plot(pr_xgb_ff, col = plot_colors[5], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[5], add = TRUE)
plot(pr_xgb_fc, col = plot_colors[6], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[6], add = TRUE)
legend("bottomleft", legend = plot_legends, col = plot_colors, lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines, cex = 0.7)

# Plot 3: F1 Score vs. Cutoff Threshold
plot(f1_ff, col = plot_colors[1], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[1], main = "F1 Score vs. Cutoff Threshold",
     ylim = c(0, 1), ylab = "F1 Score", xlab = "Probability Threshold")
plot(f1_fc, col = plot_colors[2], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[2], add = TRUE)
plot(f1_best_ff, col = plot_colors[3], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[3], add = TRUE)
plot(f1_best_fc, col = plot_colors[4], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[4], add = TRUE)
plot(f1_xgb_ff, col = plot_colors[5], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[5], add = TRUE)
plot(f1_xgb_fc, col = plot_colors[6], lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines[6], add = TRUE)
legend("bottomleft", legend = plot_legends, col = plot_colors, lwd = 2, lty = plot_lines, cex = 0.7)
```

## P Quartiles and Thresholds

```{r}
library(xtable)
library(dplyr)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Generate XGBoost Predictions
# Note: XGBoost requires the DMatrix objects (dtest, dtest_college)
# ==============================================================================

test_gbm$p_xgb = predict(xgb_model, newdata = dtest)
test_college$p_xgb = predict(xgb_model, newdata = dtest_college)

# ==============================================================================
# 2. Create Population Quartiles
# ==============================================================================

test_gbm$p_xgb_quartiles <- cut(
  test_gbm$p_xgb, 
  breaks = quantile(test_gbm$p_xgb, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)), 
  labels = c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"), 
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

test_college$p_xgb_quartiles <- cut(
  test_college$p_xgb, 
  breaks = quantile(test_college$p_xgb, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1)), 
  labels = c("Q1", "Q2", "Q3", "Q4"), 
  include.lowest = TRUE
)

# Check the distributions
table(test_gbm$p_xgb_quartiles)
table(test_college$p_xgb_quartiles)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. Calculate True Positive Proportions per Quartile
# ==============================================================================

quartiles_table_xgb_ff <- test_gbm %>%
  group_by(p_xgb_quartiles) %>%
  summarise(
    count = sum(undocu_likely == 1),
    n = n(),
    actual_proportion = (count / n)
  )

quartiles_table_xgb_fc <- test_college %>%
  group_by(p_xgb_quartiles) %>%
  summarise(
    count = sum(undocu_likely == 1),
    n = n(),
    actual_proportion = (count / n)
  )

print("=== XGBoost: Full to Full Quartiles ===")
print(quartiles_table_xgb_ff)
xtable(quartiles_table_xgb_ff, digits=4)

print("=== XGBoost: Full to College Quartiles ===")
print(quartiles_table_xgb_fc)
xtable(quartiles_table_xgb_fc, digits=4)

# ==============================================================================
# 4. Calculate 75% Recall Thresholds
# ==============================================================================

top_75_sample_xgb_ff <- test_gbm %>%
  filter(undocu_likely == 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(p_xgb)) %>%
  mutate(
    rank = row_number(),
    cumulative_p = rank / n(),
    top_75 = cumulative_p <= 0.75
  ) %>%
  filter(top_75 == TRUE)

threshold_75_xgb_ff <- min(top_75_sample_xgb_ff$p_xgb)

top_75_sample_xgb_fc <- test_college %>%
  filter(undocu_likely == 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(p_xgb)) %>%
  mutate(
    rank = row_number(),
    cumulative_p = rank / n(),
    top_75 = cumulative_p <= 0.75
  ) %>%
  filter(top_75 == TRUE)

threshold_75_xgb_fc <- min(top_75_sample_xgb_fc$p_xgb)

# Create XGBoost high recall class predictions
test_gbm$predicted_class_xgb <- ifelse(test_gbm$p_xgb >= threshold_75_xgb_ff, 1, 0)
test_college$predicted_class_xgb <- ifelse(test_college$p_xgb >= threshold_75_xgb_fc, 1, 0)

# ==============================================================================
# 5. Calculate Quartiles Specifically for the Positive Class (Undocumented)
# ==============================================================================

undocu_test_xgb_ff <- test_gbm %>%
  filter(undocu_likely == 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(p_xgb))

undocu_test_xgb_fc <- test_college %>%
  filter(undocu_likely == 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(p_xgb))

quartile_thresholds_xgb_ff <- quantile(undocu_test_xgb_ff$p_xgb, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))
print("=== XGBoost Positive-Class Thresholds (Full-Full) ===")
print(quartile_thresholds_xgb_ff)

quartile_thresholds_xgb_fc <- quantile(undocu_test_xgb_fc$p_xgb, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))
print("=== XGBoost Positive-Class Thresholds (Full-College) ===")
print(quartile_thresholds_xgb_fc)

# ==============================================================================
# MISSING STEP: Calculate Thresholds for Best GBM Model
# ==============================================================================
library(dplyr)

# 1. Generate predictions for the best_model on the test set
test_gbm$p_best <- predict(best_model, newdata = test_gbm, 
                           type = "response", n.trees = best_params$optimal_trees)

# 2. Calculate the 75% Recall Threshold (Full to Full)
top_75_sample_best_ff <- test_gbm %>%
  filter(undocu_likely == 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(p_best)) %>%
  mutate(
    rank = row_number(),
    cumulative_p = rank / n(),
    top_75 = cumulative_p <= 0.75
  ) %>%
  filter(top_75 == TRUE)

threshold_75_best_ff <- min(top_75_sample_best_ff$p_best)

# 3. Calculate Positive-Class Quartiles (Full to Full)
undocu_test_best_ff <- test_gbm %>%
  filter(undocu_likely == 1) %>%
  arrange(desc(p_best))

quartile_thresholds_best_ff <- quantile(undocu_test_best_ff$p_best, probs = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1))

# Check the values
cat("Best GBM 75% Threshold:", threshold_75_best_ff, "\n")
print("Best GBM Quartiles:")
print(quartile_thresholds_best_ff)
```

## Imputations

```{r Undocu imputation}
library(dplyr)
library(xgboost)

# ==============================================================================
# 1. Prep ACS Data for XGBoost
# ==============================================================================
# Create the numeric matrix using the exact same columns used in training
acs_matrix <- ACS %>% 
  select(age, fem, married, cit_spouse, medicaid, nonfluent, 
         spanish_hispanic_latino, central_latino, bpl_asia, household_size, 
         poverty, asian, black, white, other_race, employed, years_us, yrsed) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric)) %>% 
  as.matrix()

# Since ACS doesn't have the labels yet, we omit the 'label' argument
dacs <- xgb.DMatrix(data = acs_matrix)


# ==============================================================================
# 2. Impute Predictions and Quartiles into ACS
# ==============================================================================
setwd(data_path)

ACS <- ACS %>%
  mutate(
    # --- 1. Base GBM Model ---
    gbm_undocu_p = predict(gbm_model, newdata = ACS, n.trees = optimal_trees_gbm, type = "response"),
    
    gbm_undocu_q = case_when(
      gbm_undocu_p < quartile_thresholds_gbm[2] ~ "Q1",
      gbm_undocu_p >= quartile_thresholds_gbm[2] & gbm_undocu_p < quartile_thresholds_gbm[3] ~ "Q2",
      gbm_undocu_p >= quartile_thresholds_gbm[3] & gbm_undocu_p < quartile_thresholds_gbm[4] ~ "Q3",
      gbm_undocu_p >= quartile_thresholds_gbm[4] ~ "Q4",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    gbm_high_prob = ifelse(gbm_undocu_q == "Q4", 1, 0),
    gbm_low_prob = ifelse(gbm_undocu_q == "Q1", 1, 0),
    gbm_high_recall = ifelse(gbm_undocu_p >= threshold_75_num, 1, 0),


    # --- 2. Best GBM Model (From Grid Search) ---
    best_gbm_undocu_p = predict(best_model, newdata = ACS, n.trees = best_params$optimal_trees, type = "response"),
    
    # Assuming you created 'quartile_thresholds_best_ff' and 'threshold_75_best_ff' in the previous step
    # If not, you can swap these out for the base thresholds for comparison
    best_gbm_undocu_q = case_when(
      best_gbm_undocu_p < quartile_thresholds_best_ff[2] ~ "Q1",
      best_gbm_undocu_p >= quartile_thresholds_best_ff[2] & best_gbm_undocu_p < quartile_thresholds_best_ff[3] ~ "Q2",
      best_gbm_undocu_p >= quartile_thresholds_best_ff[3] & best_gbm_undocu_p < quartile_thresholds_best_ff[4] ~ "Q3",
      best_gbm_undocu_p >= quartile_thresholds_best_ff[4] ~ "Q4",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    best_gbm_high_prob = ifelse(best_gbm_undocu_q == "Q4", 1, 0),
    best_gbm_low_prob = ifelse(best_gbm_undocu_q == "Q1", 1, 0),
    best_gbm_high_recall = ifelse(best_gbm_undocu_p >= threshold_75_best_ff, 1, 0),


    # --- 3. XGBoost Model ---
    # predict() here uses the dacs matrix we created at the top
    xgb_undocu_p = predict(xgb_model, newdata = dacs),
    
    xgb_undocu_q = case_when(
      xgb_undocu_p < quartile_thresholds_xgb_ff[2] ~ "Q1",
      xgb_undocu_p >= quartile_thresholds_xgb_ff[2] & xgb_undocu_p < quartile_thresholds_xgb_ff[3] ~ "Q2",
      xgb_undocu_p >= quartile_thresholds_xgb_ff[3] & xgb_undocu_p < quartile_thresholds_xgb_ff[4] ~ "Q3",
      xgb_undocu_p >= quartile_thresholds_xgb_ff[4] ~ "Q4",
      TRUE ~ "Unknown"
    ),
    xgb_high_prob = ifelse(xgb_undocu_q == "Q4", 1, 0),
    xgb_low_prob = ifelse(xgb_undocu_q == "Q1", 1, 0),
    xgb_high_recall = ifelse(xgb_undocu_p >= threshold_75_xgb_ff, 1, 0)
  )

# ==============================================================================
# 3. Output Checks
# ==============================================================================

# write.csv(ACS, "ACS_SIPP_imputed_all_models.csv", row.names = FALSE)

print("=== Base GBM Quartile Distribution ===")
print(table(ACS$gbm_undocu_q))

print("=== Best GBM Quartile Distribution ===")
print(table(ACS$best_gbm_undocu_q))

print("=== XGBoost Quartile Distribution ===")
print(table(ACS$xgb_undocu_q))
```

# Diagnostics

```{r}
cat("\n--- TOP 5 PREDICTORS: CLASS & DISTRIBUTION COMPARISON ---\n")

# 2. Safely compare classes and distributions without crashing
for (var in top_15_vars) {
  cat("\n========================================\n")
  cat("VARIABLE:", toupper(var), "\n")
  
  # Check Classes
  sipp_class <- class(train_gbm[[var]])[1]
  acs_class <- class(ACS[[var]])[1]
  cat("SIPP Trained As :", sipp_class, "\n")
  cat("ACS Currently Is:", acs_class, "\n\n")
  
  # Compare Distributions
  if (sipp_class %in% c("numeric", "integer")) {
    cat("-> Numeric Comparison (Means):\n")
    cat("   SIPP:", round(mean(train_gbm[[var]], na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
    cat("   ACS :", round(mean(ACS[[var]], na.rm = TRUE), 4), "\n")
  } else {
    cat("-> Categorical Comparison (Top Proportions):\n")
    cat("   SIPP:\n")
    print(head(sort(prop.table(table(train_gbm[[var]], useNA = "ifany")), decreasing = TRUE), 3))
    cat("   ACS:\n")
    print(head(sort(prop.table(table(ACS[[var]], useNA = "ifany")), decreasing = TRUE), 3))
  }
}
```
